daemons_per_root._why: one daemon per project root (lib/util/registry daemonsFor, no scan): a second is the lifecycle fault the soak exists to catch; 0 during a restart is fine

reconnect_failures._why: every dropped surface socket gets its hello back within 5 s (drive.js RECONNECT_MS)

restart_failures._why: every restart (stop.js then start.js, each 5 minutes) answers within 10 s (drive.js RESTART_MS)

write_failures._why: no render, markdown, element, spawn/close or turn write the drive makes is refused or lost

script_errors._why: no pane script throws at mount (kind script-error in the event log since the soak began)

viewers._why: the daemon counts exactly the drive's sockets: a socket that outlives its close is a leak (scripts/soak/lib.js DRIVE_SOCKETS, read at run time)

mirror_parsed._why: the parsed-conversation budget holds: never more conversations parsed than the retention table's parsed-conversations-max (lib/server/mirror/retention.js valueOf, read at run time)

mirror_watchers._why: the chat mirror's file watches (mirror.stats().watchers) follow the conversations it has parsed — calibration: 0 → 3, one per conversation read — and drive.js reads one conversation a cycle and restarts the daemon every DRIVE_RESTART_EVERY cycles, so a daemon holds at most that many plus WATCH_SLACK (scripts/soak/lib.js, read at run time); a watch kept past its conversation, or re-made per reconnect, exceeds it

heap_used_mb._why: heap is load-sensitive, so judged by slope (MB per minute, least squares over the soak); calibration: 36.2 → 30.0, slope -1.97/min over 3 minutes. The restarts every 5 minutes reset it: a climb inside each daemon life that a restart wipes is not a slope across the soak (see the U579 hand-off)

handles._why: active resources of the daemon process (sockets, file watches, timers), last sample against first. Calibration (3 min, 3 cycles, no restart): 5 → 10, one watch per conversation read plus in-flight sockets; a daemon life holds at most 5 reads, so a fresh start against a full life is ≈ +8, and 15 leaves room for the requests in flight at a sample

timers._why: Timeout entries of the daemon process: a pane, a socket or a turn that leaves a timer behind grows it. Calibration: 3 → 5 over 3 reads in one daemon life

mirror_timers._why: the chat mirror's own timers (mirror.stats().timers); calibration: 2 → 1
